text:
kendra: thinking out loud — we should consider steering fairness at the ingress layer instead of relying on downstream admission. a short-term tweak: proportional steering with tenant weight + recent-usage decay. avoids hot-tenant starvation.

dmitri: +1. curious how this interacts with KV prefetch on stream resume though — prefetch can spike a shard.

maya: yeah that spike is the kicker. onboarding a resumed stream currently triggers a full prefix fetch. we should limit prefetch concurrency per-tenant or per-conn.

ingress-bot: current SLOs: 99.9% 95th latency under 200ms for small streams. recent load shows 2x latency increase when resume-prefetch > 16 concurrent. (logs: /var/log/ingress/prefetch-2026-03.gz)

rachel: proposal: steering policy decides target upstream (fast/cheap) then ingress enforces a prefetch budget tied to that steering decision. e.g. if steered to cheap-backend, prefetch_budget=2, if to premium, budget=8. keeps fairness and cost control.

kendra: that seems reasonable. also think about offering a tiny prefetch (first 8 tokens) synchronous + background async for the rest. reduces tail latency for common prefixes.

dmitri: we should cap background async jobs per-instance and use a tokenized evict window instead of count-based. memory grows with sequence length, not requests.

maya: config sketch:
```yaml
steering_policy:
  mode: proportional_decay
  decay_seconds: 60
  tenant_weight_key: quota_weight
prefetch:
  sync_tokens: 8
  async_budget_by_backend:
    premium: 8
    standard: 2
  max_async_per_instance: 32
  eviction: token_window: 65536
```

rachel: also add telemetry hooks: per-tenant prefetch_hits, async_drop_rate, and downstream_fallback_rate so we can A/B safely.

kendra: ops question — if background async fails, do we immediate-fallback to hedging/secondary model, or allow graceful degrade?

dmitri: prefer graceful degrade + signal to router to reduce weight for that backend for a short window. avoid immediate hedging on every miss.

ingress-bot: note: will emit event `prefetch.async.drop` with tags {tenant, backend, instance} when async gets throttled.

maya: follow-up task: add quota check at steering time (before selecting backend) so we don't steer + prefetch for tenants over quota. I'll open a tiny RFC.

kendra: thanks. can someone write up a short follow-up doc with config defaults and metrics to watch? i can review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
